name: Salsa macha
intro: One jar. The poblano, dried, fried, and kept.
card_uses: Stir it into beans, oil and all.
Put it on a fried egg.
Set it on the table next to anything braised.
ingredients: 3 ancho chiles, stemmed, seeded, and torn into pieces
6–10 chiles de árbol, stemmed (fewer if you're careful)
method: Put the oil, garlic, and peanuts in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook gently, stirring now and then, until the garlic is pale gold and crisp, about eight minutes — not brown. Add the sesame seeds for one minute. Take the pan off the heat, then add the chiles and stir: the oil is hot enough to toast them without burning them, and burnt chiles are the one way to ruin this. Let it sit five minutes. Pour everything into a blender with the salt, sugar, and vinegar, and pulse a few times — it should stay chunky, like gravel in oil, not smooth. Cool completely, then jar it. The idea underneath is worth keeping: fry the aromatics gently, take it off the heat, and let the leftover heat toast the chiles. It works with any dried chile you find.

storage.note: Keep it in the fridge, with the solids under the oil. It's best in the first two weeks and good for a month. The oil firms up cold; let it sit out ten minutes before using. Always use a clean spoon.
